grammar: A compact greeting, followed here by an invitation to enter.
note: 小林 is a person's name; 请进 qǐng jìn means please come in. Connected speech: 你好 is normally pronounced ní hǎo; the reading retains lexical tones.

grammar: 我 refers to the person speaking.
note: 叫 jiào means be called; 林安 Lín Ān is a person's name.

grammar: 你 addresses the person being spoken to.
note: 是 shì links a person to an identity; final 吗 ma makes this a yes/no question. 林安 is a person's name.

grammar: 他 refers back to 林先生.
note: 这是 zhè shì means this is; 林先生 Lín xiānsheng means Mr Lin. 先生 identifies the male referent here.

grammar: 她 refers back to 王女士. 她 and 他 have the same pronunciation.
note: 王女士 Wáng nǚshì means Ms Wang; 王宁 Wáng Níng is her full name. 女士 identifies the female referent here.

grammar: A name follows 叫 when asking what someone is called.
note: 小安 Xiǎo Ān is a familiar form of address.

grammar: 你的 means your; 的 de connects the person to the name.
note: The second syllable zi is neutral-tone.

grammar: A family name follows 姓. 林 is the family name in 林安.
谁 asks for a person's identity; this question does not need 吗.
note: 这位先生 zhè wèi xiānsheng means this gentleman. shéi is an everyday spoken reading of 谁.

grammar: 是 links 我 to the identifying name 林安.
Final 吗 turns the statement 你姓王 into a yes/no question.
note: 吗 is neutral-tone. 王 Wáng is a family name.

grammar: 不 comes before 姓 to deny the proposed surname.
note: Connected speech: 不姓 is normally bú xìng because 姓 has fourth tone. The target reading retains lexical bù.

grammar: 什么名字 asks what name someone has; no 吗 is added.
note: The second syllable me is neutral-tone.

grammar: 是什么意思 asks what something means.
note: 这个 zhè ge means this before a noun; ge is neutral-tone here. 这个名字 means this name. The second syllable si in 意思 is neutral-tone.

grammar: 汉字 can refer to one Chinese character or to Chinese characters generally.
note: The quotation marks identify 林 as the written character being discussed.
说 shuō means speak here; 说中文 means speak Chinese.

grammar: The words after the colon are what 王女士 says.
请 comes before the requested action to make a polite request.
再 comes before 说 to request another saying of the words.
note: 没听清 méi tīngqīng means did not catch what was said. 一遍 yī biàn means once through; connected speech here is yí biàn. These are supported chunks.

grammar: 说慢一点 is a supported request meaning speak a little more slowly.
note: 一点 yīdiǎn means a little here; connected speech is yìdiǎn. Learn the request as a short useful frame.

grammar: A compact expression of thanks in response to an invitation.
note: The second syllable xie is neutral-tone.

grammar: A compact conventional reply to thanks.
note: The syllable qi is neutral-tone. Connected speech: 不客气 is normally bú kèqi because 客 has fourth tone.

sentence: “对不起，请再说一遍。”“我叫林安。”
grammar: The apology politely prefaces a request to repeat a name.
note: The middle syllable bu is neutral-tone in this fixed expression.

sentence: “对不起，我没听清。”“没关系，我再说一遍。”
grammar: A compact reassuring response to an apology.
note: The final syllable xi is neutral-tone. The speaker follows the reassurance by offering to repeat.

grammar: 好 accepts the request before the speaker repeats their name.

sentence: 小安，我们明天见面，好吗？
grammar: 见面 describes people meeting each other. 好吗 asks whether the suggestion is all right.
note: 我们 wǒmen means we; 明天 míngtiān means tomorrow.

grammar: 我的 means my, using the possessive pattern already seen in 你的.
note: The second syllable you is neutral-tone.
老师 can also follow a family name as a form of address, as in 林老师, Teacher Lin.

grammar: 林老师 addresses Teacher Lin directly.
note: The second syllable sheng is neutral-tone in this standard spoken reading.

grammar: A compact farewell in an exchange between a teacher and a student.
note: 明天见 míngtiān jiàn means see you tomorrow.
鸭 yā means duck. The initial in 鸡 is written j in Pinyin.

sentence: 我知道你的名字，你叫林安。
grammar: 知道 takes the information known: here, someone's name.
note: The first initial is zh; the second syllable dao is neutral-tone.
号码 hàomǎ means an assigned number. The initial in 七 is written q in Pinyin.

grammar: 吃 is followed by the food being eaten.
note: 面 miàn means noodles here. The initial in 吃 is written ch, contrasting with q in 七.

grammar: 小 describes size directly in this question.
note: 这只猫 zhè zhī māo means this cat; 只 is a classifier for animals. The initial in 小 is written x.

grammar: 少 describes the number of friends.
note: 太 tài means too, indicating an excessive degree. The initial sh in 少 contrasts with x in 小.

grammar: 太早吗 asks whether the proposed time is too early.
note: 七点 qī diǎn means seven o'clock. The initial in 早 is written z.

grammar: 找 is followed by the person being sought.
note: Initial zh contrasts with z in 早. Connected speech: within 找小安, 找 normally has a rising realization before third-tone 小, giving zháo xiǎo. The preceding 我 depends on phrase grouping. The target reading retains lexical zhǎo.

grammar: 擦 is followed by the surface to be wiped.
note: 桌子 zhuōzi means table; zi is neutral-tone. The initial in 擦 is written c, contrasting with ch in 吃.
喝 hē means drink; 请喝茶 is a polite offer of tea. Initial ch in 茶 contrasts with c in 擦.
The initial in 三 is s, contrasting with sh in 山 shān.
那 nà means that. 山 shān begins with sh; 三 sān begins with s.

sentence: 我们七月三日见面，好吗？
grammar: 日 follows the day number in this calendar date.
register: Calendar-style date wording; everyday conversation also commonly uses 号.
note: 七月三日 qī yuè sān rì means July 3; 月 yuè marks the month and 三 sān means three. In rì, the spelling i follows r and differs from the i in jī.

grammar: 太热 means too hot.
note: 这杯茶 zhè bēi chá means this cup of tea; 杯 measures a cupful here. 热 begins with r.

grammar: 这个字 refers to this written character.
note: In zì, i follows z and differs from the i in jī. 字 is a complete noun here.

grammar: 一次 means one time; 次 counts occurrences of an action.
note: 一 yī means one. Connected speech: 一次 is normally yí cì because 次 has fourth tone. In cì, i follows c.

grammar: 四点 means four o'clock.
note: In sì, i follows s and differs from the i in qī.

grammar: 一张纸 means one sheet of paper.
note: 给 gěi means give; 张 zhāng counts sheets here. The initial in 纸 is zh, followed by the special i spelling.
The first syllable begins with ch; the second syllable zi is neutral-tone. Each i follows its own initial, ch or z.

grammar: 十个学生 means ten students; 个 is a general counting word.
note: 有 yǒu means have. The i in shí follows sh and differs from the i in qī.

grammar: 那个人 means that person.
note: 那 nà means that; 个 is the counting word in this phrase and is commonly unstressed. 人 begins with r.
肉 begins with r; its final is written ou.
The second syllable ròu begins with r. 牛肉 is the complete word for beef.

grammar: 一个橘子 means one orange.
note: After j, Pinyin writes ü as u, so jú contains ü despite the missing dots. The second syllable zi is neutral-tone.

grammar: The destination 学校 follows 去.
note: 学校 xuéxiào means school. After q, Pinyin writes ü as u; qù does not have the u of shū.
书 has initial sh followed by u, unlike the ü written u after j or q.

grammar: 外面有… asks whether something is present outside.
note: 外面 wàimiàn means outside; 有 yǒu means there is here. After x, Pinyin omits the dots from ü, giving the spelling xue.
太热 tài rè means too hot. 水 begins with sh; the u in its final ui belongs to the u series, unlike the ü in xuě.

grammar: 我家 means my home; 的 is normally omitted in this familiar combination.
note: 来 lái means come. 来我家喝茶 means come to my home for tea. 家 begins with j.

grammar: 这张桌子 means this table; 张 is a classifier used with tables.
note: The first syllable begins with zh; the second syllable zi is neutral-tone.
The complete word contains q in qǐ and ch in chuáng. Connected speech: qǐ before second-tone chuáng normally stays low; its lexical third tone is retained in the reading.
那 nà means that. 车 refers to a car here and begins with ch.

grammar: 在…下 means be under something; 下 follows the object used as the location reference.
note: 书 shū means book; 在 zài introduces its location. 下 begins with x, contrasting with sh in 上 shàng.

grammar: 在…上 means be on something; 上 follows the object used as the location reference.
note: 尺子 chǐzi means ruler; 在 zài introduces its location. 上 begins with sh, contrasting with x in 下 xià.

grammar: 认识 takes a person here; it asks about acquaintance rather than knowing a fact.
note: The first syllable begins with r; the second syllable shi is neutral-tone.

grammar: 女的 describes a female person here; final 的 de completes this descriptive frame.
note: Pinyin keeps the ü dots after n, as in nǚ.

grammar: 我会努力 is a short promise meaning I will make an effort. 会 huì marks the future commitment here.
note: The first syllable nǔ has u, contrasting with ü in nǚ. Connected speech: nǔ before fourth-tone lì normally stays low; the reading retains lexical third tone.

grammar: 是绿的 states the car's color; 的 de completes this descriptive frame.
note: 车 chē means car. Pinyin keeps the ü dots after l, as in lǜ.

grammar: 这条路 means this road; 条 tiáo is the classifier used here.
note: 很长 hěn cháng means long. 路 lù has u, contrasting with ü in 绿 lǜ.

grammar: 这条鱼 means this fish; 条 tiáo is a classifier used with fish.
note: 很小 hěn xiǎo means small. Pinyin writes the ü sound as yu when no consonant initial precedes it.
那只 nà zhī means that before an animal noun. 猪 has zh followed by u, contrasting with the ü represented by yu in 鱼.

grammar: 饿 directly describes the listener's state; 是 is not needed.
note: 饿 has the final e and lexical fourth tone.
鹅 é and 饿 è share the final e but have different lexical tones.

grammar: 是破的 describes the paper's damaged condition; 的 de completes this descriptive frame.
note: 这张纸 zhè zhāng zhǐ means this sheet of paper. Pinyin writes the final after p as o in pò.
The first syllable has the final uo. The second syllable bo is neutral-tone.

sentence: 小安，你的狗叫什么名字？
note: 狗 has the final ou. Connected speech: 狗 before fourth-tone 叫 normally stays low rather than having a full fall-and-rise.

grammar: 很多 describes a large number; 很 need not carry a strong very meaning in this ordinary statement.
note: 书 shū means book; 很 hěn supports the adjective statement. 多 has the final uo and contrasts in quantity with 少 shǎo.

grammar: 什么 before 豆 asks what kind of bean this is.
note: 豆 dòu has the final ou, contrasting with uo in 多 duō.

grammar: 在桌子上 means on the table.
note: 饭 refers to the prepared meal here. 在 zài introduces location; 上 shàng means on. 饭 has the final an.

grammar: 一间房 means one room; 间 jiān is a classifier for rooms.
register: Polite request at an accommodation reception.
note: 给 gěi means give; 给我 means give me. 房 has the final ang, contrasting with an in 饭 fàn.

grammar: 是蓝的 states the paper's color.
note: 蓝 has the final an.

grammar: 这张图上 means in this picture; 一只 counts one animal.
note: 图 tú means picture. 狼 láng has final ang, contrasting with an in 蓝 lán.

grammar: 学校的门 means the school's door.
note: 门 has the final en.

grammar: 很冷 describes the temperature outside.
note: 冷 has the final eng. 请进 qǐng jìn means please come in.

grammar: 在盆里 means in the basin; 里 lǐ means inside.
note: 盆 has the final en.
灯 has final eng, contrasting with en in 盆 pén.

grammar: 新 directly describes the car; 是 is not needed.
note: 新 has the final in.

grammar: 天上 tiānshàng means in the sky; 很多 means many.
note: The first syllable has final ing, contrasting with in in 新 xīn. The second syllable xing is neutral-tone.

grammar: 离 lí introduces the reference place: 我家离学校很近 means the speaker's home is near the school.
note: 近 has the final in.
The first syllable has final ing, contrasting with in in 近 jìn. The second syllable zi is neutral-tone.

grammar: 天 is the complete noun sky here, followed by its description.
note: 蓝 lán means blue. 天 has the final ian.
姜 names the food ingredient and has final iang, contrasting with ian in 天 tiān.

grammar: 面 is the complete food noun following 吃.
note: 面 means noodles here and has the final ian.

grammar: 这杯水 means this cup of water.
note: 凉 describes the water's temperature. Its final iang contrasts with ian in 面 miàn.

grammar: 关 takes the visible object 门, the door.
note: 冷 lěng means cold; 门 mén means door. 外面很冷 means it is cold outside. 关 has final uan.

grammar: 房里 means in the room; 里 lǐ means inside.
note: 光 means light here. Its final uang contrasts with uan in 关 guān.

grammar: 太短 means too short.
note: 短 describes the ruler's length and has the final uan.

grammar: 张 zhāng also counts beds; 这张床 means this bed.
note: 床 has final uang, contrasting with uan in 短 duǎn.

grammar: 见 is followed by the person the speaker will meet.
note: 见 has the final ian.

grammar: 想 followed by an action expresses a wish to do it.
note: 想 has final iang. Connected speech: 想 before first-tone 喝 normally stays low; the reading retains lexical third tone.

grammar: 妈 directly addresses the speaker's mother.
note: 妈 has first tone.

grammar: 麻 describes how the speaker's foot feels.
note: 脚 jiǎo means foot. 麻 má has second tone, contrasting with first-tone 妈 mā.
牛 niú means cow. 马 mǎ has lexical third tone.

grammar: 别 bié before an action means do not; 请别骂我 asks the listener not to scold the speaker.
note: 骂 has fourth tone. 没听清 means did not catch what was said.

grammar: After giving their own surname, the speaker uses 你呢 to ask for the listener's surname.
note: 呢 is neutral-tone.
The first syllable bà has fourth tone; the second ba is neutral-tone.

grammar: 妈妈 names the speaker's mother as the subject of the statement.
note: The first syllable mā has first tone; the second ma is neutral-tone.
哥哥 means an older male sibling. The second syllable ge is neutral-tone.

sentence: 这是我的姐姐，她是老师。
grammar: 姐姐 names an older female sibling; 她 refers back to her.
note: The second syllable jie is neutral-tone, so 姐姐 is not a pair of full third tones. The reading retains lexical jiě.
弟弟 means a younger male sibling. The first syllable dì has fourth tone; the second di is neutral-tone.
妹妹 means a younger female sibling. The second syllable mei is neutral-tone.

grammar: 这个孩子 means this child.
note: The first syllable hái has second tone; the second zi is neutral-tone.

sentence: 小安，你的东西在桌子下。
grammar: 你的东西 refers to the listener's belongings.
note: The second syllable xi is neutral-tone in this things sense. It is not the full-tone reading for east and west.

grammar: 吃饭的时候 is a supported frame meaning when eating a meal. 的 connects the action to the time noun 时候.
note: 说话 shuōhuà means talk. The second syllable hou in 时候 is neutral-tone.

grammar: 林老师的书 means Teacher Lin's book; 的 connects the owner to the owned item.
note: 的 is neutral-tone here.

grammar: 得 before 去 expresses necessity, motivated here by the class schedule.
note: 上课 shàngkè means have class; 七点上课 means class starts at seven. 得 is read děi here. Connected speech: děi before fourth-tone qù normally stays low.

grammar: 长 describes the ruler's length.
note: 长 is read cháng in this length sense.

grammar: 长大 is the complete word grow up, with 长 read zhǎng.
note: 想 xiǎng means want to; 快点 kuài diǎn means sooner here. Connected speech: zhǎng before fourth-tone dà normally stays low; the reading retains lexical third tone.

grammar: 行吗 asks whether the visible meeting arrangement is acceptable.
note: 行 is read xíng in this acceptability sense.

grammar: 在学校旁边 locates the bank beside the school.
note: 旁边 pángbiān means beside. In 银行, 行 is read háng; 银行 is the complete word bank.

grammar: 还 before 在学校 says that 小安 continues to be at school.
note: 四点了 means it is four o'clock now; learn it as a short time-update chunk. 还 is read hái in this still sense.

grammar: 还 takes the visible object 我的书, my book.
note: 还 is read huán when returning an object, unlike hái meaning still.

grammar: 什么乐器 asks what kind of musical instrument this is.
note: In the complete word 乐器, 乐 is read yuè.

grammar: 快乐 describes how 小安 feels at school.
note: In 快乐, 乐 is read lè, contrasting with yuè in 乐器.

grammar: 太重 means too heavy and describes the table's weight.
note: 重 is read zhòng in this weight sense.

grammar: 重新 before 写 requests a fresh attempt at writing.
note: 对 duì means correct; 写 xiě means write. 重 is read chóng in 重新. Connected speech: 不对 is normally bú duì.

grammar: 几 comes before the counting word 个 to ask for a number, usually when a relatively small count is expected.
note: 几 has lexical third tone in this number question.

grammar: 三年 means three years and gives the intended length of study.
note: 学 xué means study. 年 has second tone and functions as a complete time unit here.

grammar: 本 stands between the number and 书: 三本书 means three books.
note: 本 is a complete grammatical counting unit here and has lexical third tone.

grammar: 看 takes 这本书 as its object and means read in this context.
note: 这本书 means this book. 看 is read kàn in this reading sense.

sentence: 今天我在家，明天去学校。
grammar: 今天 gives the time of the first statement, contrasting with 明天, tomorrow.
note: 今天 has the lexical tone pair first tone plus first tone.

grammar: 明天 places the visit on the day after today.
note: 明天 has the lexical tone pair second tone plus first tone. 你家 means your home.

sentence: 小安，后天三点来我家，好吗？
grammar: 后天 names the day after 明天.
note: 后天 has the lexical tone pair fourth tone plus first tone. 三点 means three o'clock.

grammar: 明年 places the intended study in the next calendar year.
note: 明年 has two full second-tone syllables.

grammar: 电话 names the object whose location is being given.
note: 电话 has two full fourth-tone syllables.

grammar: 学校的大门 means the school's main entrance.
note: 大门 has the lexical tone pair fourth tone plus second tone. Here it names the main entrance, rather than describing any door as large.

grammar: 想开门 expresses the speaker's wish to open the door; the room's heat gives the reason.
note: 开 kāi means open; 门 mén means door. This first-plus-second tone combination has a verb and its object, written as separate Pinyin words.

grammar: The speaker contrasts not wanting tea with wanting to drink water.
note: 喝 has first tone and 水 has lexical third tone. The verb and its object are separate Pinyin words.

grammar: 吃饭前 means before eating a meal; 前 qián means before here.
note: Connected speech: within 洗手, the first third tone normally becomes rising, giving xí shǒu. The reading keeps lexical xǐ shǒu, with the verb and object separated.

grammar: 水果 is the desired food, contrasted with noodles.
note: Connected speech: the first of the two third tones normally becomes rising, giving shuíguǒ. The reading retains lexical shuǐguǒ.

grammar: 在床上 means on the bed.
note: Connected speech: the first third tone in 手表 normally becomes rising, giving shóubiǎo. The reading retains lexical shǒubiǎo.

sentence: 林老师，上课的时候可以喝水吗？
grammar: 可以 before 喝水 asks permission to drink water. 上课的时候 means during class.
note: Connected speech: within 可以, the first third tone normally becomes rising, giving kéyǐ. The reading retains lexical kěyǐ.

grammar: 很 comes before 好 hǎo, good, in this positive assessment. In an ordinary adjective statement, it need not strongly emphasize very.
note: Connected speech: 很好 is normally hén hǎo because two third tones meet across the words. The target reading retains lexical hěn.

grammar: 买 takes the visible object 书; 去买书 means go to buy books.
note: Connected speech: 买 before first-tone 书 normally stays low, without a full fall-and-rise. The reading retains lexical mǎi.

grammar: 米饭 names cooked rice as the food the speaker wants.
note: Connected speech: in this third-plus-fourth tone word, mǐ normally stays low before fàn. The reading retains lexical mǐfàn.

grammar: 在北京 gives the location of the speaker's home.
note: The city name is capitalized in Pinyin. Connected speech: Běi normally stays low before first-tone jīng; the reading retains lexical third tone.

grammar: 坐 zuò means travel by here; 坐火车去北京 means go to Beijing by train.
note: Connected speech: huǒ normally stays low before first-tone chē. The reading retains the lexical third-plus-first tone combination huǒchē.

grammar: The teacher asks the named student to stand up.
note: Connected speech: qǐ normally stays low before fourth-tone lì. The reading retains the lexical third-plus-fourth tone combination qǐlì.

grammar: 那个小孩 means that child. 小孩 is an everyday alternative to 孩子.
note: Connected speech: xiǎo normally stays low before second-tone hái. Unlike háizi, xiǎohái has two full lexical tones.

grammar: 好吃 describes the food as pleasant to eat.
note: Connected speech: hǎo normally stays low before first-tone chī. The reading retains lexical hǎochī. The preceding 很 follows the third-tone change already illustrated in 很好.

grammar: 牛奶 is what the speaker does not drink; the second clause says that the speaker drinks water instead.
note: 牛奶 has the lexical tone pair second tone plus third tone; 奶 is not neutral-tone.

grammar: 在床下 means under the bed.
note: 皮带 has two full syllables with the lexical tone pair second tone plus fourth tone.

grammar: 哥哥的电脑 means older brother's computer.
note: 电脑 has the lexical tone pair fourth tone plus third tone; both syllables keep full lexical tones.

grammar: 在银行旁边 means beside the bank.
note: 医院 has the lexical tone pair first tone plus fourth tone. Its first character is 医, not the numeral 一.

sentence: 学校离我家很近，我想走路去。
grammar: 学校离我家很近 means the school is near my home. 走路去 means go there on foot.
note: Connected speech: zǒu normally stays low before fourth-tone lù. The reading retains lexical zǒulù.

grammar: 一个橘子 means one tangerine; 个 is the general counting word.
note: Connected speech: 一个 is normally yí ge here. 一 changes before the classifier's underlying fourth tone, while 个 is commonly weak and neutral. The reading retains lexical yī gè.

grammar: 住 zhù means stay here; 住一天 means stay for one day.
note: Connected speech: 一 before first-tone 天 normally becomes fourth-tone yì, giving yì tiān. The reading retains lexical yī tiān.

grammar: 学一年中文 means study Chinese for one year. 行吗 asks whether the proposal is acceptable.
note: Connected speech: 一 before second-tone 年 normally becomes fourth-tone yì, giving yì nián. The reading retains lexical yī nián.

grammar: 一本 counts one book; the noun 书 remains visible after the counting phrase.
note: Connected speech: 一 before third-tone 本 normally becomes fourth-tone yì, giving yì běn. The reading retains lexical yī běn.

grammar: 第一 gives the book's position in an ordered set; 本 remains the book classifier.
note: 一 keeps first tone in this ordinal, including before 本 here. Standard Pinyin connects the ordinal prefix dì to the numeral with a hyphen: dì-yī.

grammar: 十一 gives the speaker's assigned number.
note: Connected speech: final 一 keeps first-tone yī in this number. 十一 is written as one Pinyin word.

sentence: 我们的名字一样，都叫林安。
grammar: 一样 says that the speakers have the same name.
note: 都 dōu means both here; 都叫林安 means both are called 林安. Connected speech: 一 before fourth-tone 样 normally becomes rising, giving yíyàng. The reading retains lexical yīyàng.

sentence: 小安，明天我们一起去学校，好吗？
grammar: 一起 before 去 says that the people will go together.
note: Connected speech: 一 before third-tone 起 normally becomes fourth-tone, giving yìqǐ. The reading retains lexical yīqǐ.

sentence: 我想喝一点水，不想喝茶。
grammar: 一点水 means a little water. Here 一点 gives the amount, rather than a clock time.
note: Connected speech: 一 becomes fourth-tone yì before lexical third-tone 点. In 一点水, 点 also normally becomes rising before third-tone 水, giving yìdián shuǐ. The target reading retains lexical yīdiǎn, joined for this small-quantity expression.

sentence: 林老师，请看一下我的名字，对吗？
grammar: 请看一下 asks someone to take a brief look. Learn 看一下 as a useful request frame; 对吗 asks whether the written name is correct.
note: Connected speech: 一 before fourth-tone 下 normally becomes rising, giving yíxià. The reading retains lexical yīxià.

meaning: am not; is not; are not
grammar: 不是 denies the visible identity 老师; the second clause supplies the correct identity.
note: Connected speech: 不 before fourth-tone 是 normally becomes rising, giving bú shì. The reading retains lexical bù shì as two Pinyin words.

grammar: 不要 before the object 茶 means do not want here. The speaker states their own choice.
note: Connected speech: 不 before fourth-tone 要 normally becomes rising, giving bú yào. The reading retains lexical bù yào.

grammar: 不来 denies the planned coming; 明天 makes the time explicit.
note: Connected speech: 不 keeps fourth tone before second-tone 来 here, giving bù lái.

grammar: 不吃 is followed by the food 鱼; the visible request names cooked rice instead.
note: Connected speech: 不 keeps fourth tone before first-tone 吃 here, giving bù chī.

grammar: 不买 refers to the book named in the first clause; its high price motivates the decision.
note: 贵 guì means expensive; 太贵 means too expensive. Connected speech: 不 keeps fourth tone before third-tone 买 here, giving bù mǎi.

grammar: Final 吧 presents drinking tea together as a suggestion.
note: 吧 is weak and neutral-tone here; it does not carry a full lexical tone.

grammar: 我们 refers to the speaker and other people in the group.
note: The second syllable men is neutral-tone. 我们 is retrieved as a whole word.

grammar: 多少 asks the number of students without the small-number expectation often associated with 几.
note: The second syllable shao is neutral-tone in this ordinary quantity question.

grammar: 怎么 comes before the action 读 to ask how to pronounce the character.
note: 读 dú means read aloud or pronounce here. The second syllable me in 怎么 is neutral-tone.

grammar: 告诉我你的名字 means tell me your name. Learn this short frame with the person followed by the information.
note: The second syllable su is neutral-tone in this standard spoken reading.

sentence: 今天不上课，我们在家休息。
grammar: 在家休息 means rest at home. 今天不上课 says that there is no class today.
note: The second syllable xi is neutral-tone in this standard spoken reading.

grammar: 杯子 names the drinking container whose location is given.
note: The second syllable zi is neutral-tone.

sentence: 这张纸是白的，不是蓝的。
grammar: 是白的 states the paper's color; 不是蓝的 explicitly rejects blue.
note: Prominence: 白 is the corrective color in the white-versus-blue contrast and can receive emphasis. Its lexical tone remains second tone.

grammar: 先 marks washing hands as the first action; 再 zài means then before the second action.
note: Phrasing: 小安 is the address; 请先洗手 and 再吃饭 form the two action groups. The commas show these boundaries.

sentence: 我现在不喝茶，等一下再喝。
grammar: 现在 places the refusal at the present moment; the second clause postpones drinking the tea.
note: 等一下 děng yīxià means wait a moment; 等一下再喝 means drink a little later. Prominence and phrasing: 现在 contrasts with the later action, and the comma separates the present refusal from the postponement.

sentence: 这本书在我手里，是林老师的。
grammar: 这 comes before 本书 to identify the nearby book, which is explicitly in the speaker's hand.
note: 手里 shǒu lǐ means in one's hand; 在我手里 means in my hand. 林老师的 means Teacher Lin's, with the book understood.

sentence: 远处那辆车是林老师的。
grammar: 那 identifies a car farther away; 远处 makes its distance explicit.
note: 远处 yuǎnchù means in the distance; 辆 liàng counts vehicles. 林老师的 means Teacher Lin's, with the car understood.

sentence: 桌子上有三本书，你想看哪本？
grammar: 哪 comes before the classifier 本 to ask which book. The three visible books supply the choice set.
note: 哪本 means which book, with 书 understood. Connected speech: 哪本 normally has rising first syllable ná before third-tone 本; the reading retains lexical nǎ.

grammar: 在哪里 asks for a location; no 吗 is added.
note: Connected speech: the first of the two third tones in 哪里 normally becomes rising, giving nálǐ. The reading retains lexical nǎlǐ.

sentence: 我有一个姐姐，她在北京。
grammar: 有 states that the speaker has an older sister; 她 refers back to that sister.

sentence: 我没有书，今天想去买一本。
grammar: 没有 denies possession of books here. Use 没有, not 不有, for this meaning.
note: 一本 means one book, with 书 understood from the first clause.

grammar: 要 takes the visible object 这本书 and states the speaker's choice in a request.
需要 takes 水 as its object; the speaker's thirst establishes the immediate need.
note: 渴 kě means thirsty; 很渴 means very thirsty here.

grammar: 能 before 进来 asks the addressed teacher for permission to enter now.
note: 进来 jìnlái means come in; learn it as a useful entry phrase here.

grammar: 会 before 写 expresses a learned skill here. It does not mark a future promise in this sentence.
note: 写汉字 means write Chinese characters; 你呢 asks whether the listener has the same skill.

sentence: 我有两本书，你可以看一本。
grammar: Use 两 before the classifier 本 in 两本书. Counting aloud uses 二 èr for the number two.
note: Connected speech: 两本 normally begins liáng běn because two third tones meet. The reading retains lexical liǎng. 一本 means one of the books here.

grammar: 个 stands between 三 and 橘子; 三个橘子 means three tangerines.
note: Connected speech: 个 is commonly weak and neutral ge in this phrase. The reading gives lexical gè.

grammar: 杯 counts cupfuls of the drink: 两杯茶 means two cups of tea.
note: 杯 measures the tea here; 杯子 is the noun for the drinking container.

grammar: 三块 states a price of three yuan.
note: 块 names a money unit in this price; it does not mean a physical piece here.

sentence: 我想买这本书，可是没有钱。
grammar: 钱 is what the speaker lacks for the desired purchase.
note: 可是 kěshì means but; it connects the desired purchase with the lack of money.

grammar: 十元 states a price of ten yuan; 对吗 checks that the stated price is correct.
register: Standard currency wording, also usable in speech.
note: 元 is the standard unit name corresponding to the everyday spoken 块 in a price.

grammar: 几岁 asks a child's age in years; 岁 is the age unit.
register: Everyday question addressed to a young child.
note: 小朋友 xiǎopéngyou is a friendly way to address a child. 今年 jīnnián means this year.

grammar: 几点 asks the clock time of the visible activity 上课.
note: Connected speech: 几点 normally begins jí diǎn because two third tones meet. The reading retains lexical jǐ diǎn, with the numeral and time unit separated.

grammar: 请问 politely opens the question; the actual request for the bank's location remains visible.
note: Connected speech: qǐng normally stays low before fourth-tone wèn in this word. The reading retains lexical third tone.

sentence: “明天三点上课，不是七点。”“我明白，谢谢老师。”
grammar: 明白 acknowledges understanding after the teacher corrects the class time.
note: The second syllable bai is neutral-tone in this standard spoken reading.
